newsitem.title: UK: Major defends minister Soames in Gulf War row.
newsitem.headline: Major defends minister Soames in Gulf War row.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major stood firmly behind armed forces minister Nicholas Soames on Thursday as a row over the minister's handling of a controversy over the use of pesticides during the Gulf War rumbled on.

Members of the main opposition Labour party, which on Wednesday demanded Soames's resignation, returned to the attack during question time on Thrusday and were joined by the Liberal Democrats and the Scottish Nationalist Party.
But a spokesman for Major said the prime minister knew Soames would never have knowingly misled parliament. "The prime minister has got absolute confidence in Mr Soames," he said.
The opposition accuses Soames of shirking responsibility over the use of organophosphate pesticides, which have been blamed for causing veterans crippling illnesses in the 1991 Gulf War.

Soames admitted to parliament's Defence Committee on Wednesday that he had given incorrect answers to parliamentary questions on the use of organophosphates after receiving "flawed and inaccurate advice" from officials.
